# Capacity Command Center: bed utilization and length of stay on Databricks

An end-to-end Databricks build for a fictional multi-hospital health system, **Lakeshore Health (LSH)**: 8 hospitals, 52 units, 1,214 staffed beds. Case managers get a daily ranked list of inpatients likely to stay past their expected discharge date, with the reason why. Capacity leaders see where beds will run out today. Quality leaders see which hospitals and barriers drive excess days.

**All data is synthetic** (generated by notebook 01). The organization, hospital, city and code names are fictional; see [evidence/SCRUB_REPORT.md](evidence/SCRUB_REPORT.md).

## Architecture

```text
 Synthetic source extracts (UC volume)     ADT JSON events, encounter/DRG CSV, barrier JSON, staffed beds CSV, master data
          |  Auto Loader (Lakeflow Connect file ingestion), incremental, rescued data
          v
 Bronze (7 Delta tables)
          |  dedupe, conform, ADT -> stays, data quality checks
          v
 Silver  ->  Gold star schema: dim_date (fiscal year from Sep 1), dim_facility, dim_unit, dim_drg, dim_patient,
             fact_encounter, fact_barrier, fact_unit_census_day, current_inpatients
          |  Unity Catalog: comments, PHI tags, column masks, row filter, grants, lineage
          |  Metric views: los_metrics, capacity_metrics, barrier_metrics (one governed KPI definition)
          |  MLflow + UC models: long_stay_risk_model, los_days_model (@champion) -> scores every inpatient
          |  ai_query: huddle notes written from de-identified facts
          v
 bed_board (scored, PK, CDF) + unit_status  --synced-->  Lakebase Postgres (ms reads)  <-- write-back: discharge_plan, discharge_actions
          |                                                     ^
          v                                                     |
 Genie space (metric views + de-identified bed board)    Databricks App (Streamlit): Command Center, Discharge Worklist,
                                                         LOS Performance (metric views, as the signed-in user), Ask (Genie)
```

## Key results (FY2026 = Sep 2025 - Aug 2026, synthetic)

| KPI | Result |
| --- | --- |
| LOS O/E index | 1.24 system; 1.10 (BSH) to 1.34 (WCH); LMH 1.26 |
| Excess days | ~96,000 (LMH 42,369), about 263 staffed beds all year |
| Avoidable days | ~27,000; SNF placement is the top barrier (14,791 days) |
| Current inpatients at the 7:00 AM snapshot (2026-10-30) | 1,064; 95 high risk; ~262 discharges expected today |
| Long-stay classifier | Test AUC 0.722 (baseline 0.564), PR-AUC 0.41 vs 20% base rate; prospective AUC 0.68 on the current inpatients |

## How to run

1. Import the notebooks into a Databricks workspace with Unity Catalog and serverless compute.
2. Run `00` to `08` in order with the same `catalog` and `prefix` widgets (defaults in each notebook).
3. Deploy the app from `app/` (`databricks apps deploy <app-name> --source-code-path <folder>`), give the app user authorization scopes `sql` and `dashboards.genie`, and run notebook 06 Step 6 with the app's service principal ID for Lakebase access.

## Known limitations

* Ingestion uses Auto Loader on files; a managed Lakeflow Connect connector or HL7 feed is the production path.
* Silver and gold are built in notebooks; a Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipeline is the production path.
* The "expected discharges today" calibration was chosen on the same day it is evaluated (262 vs 262), so it is partly tuned.
* Group grants (notebook 04 Step 6) are skipped when the groups don't exist in the workspace.
